text: Hello Hanna, come and take a seat. What would you like to talk about today? I'm not really sure where to start. I think I'm just anxious all the time and it's got worse in September. What happened in September? I was my deputy head at my school, I've taught here for 11 years and I have loved it. And then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left. That sounds like recognition of your work. That's what everyone says, but I keep thinking they picked the wrong person. And that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing. What does it look like when that thought arrives? Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's stuff meeting in my head. What do you rehearse? Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say and what they would think of me if I got it wrong. What do you imagine, they would think? That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice ear for a teacher who can't actually read. Has anyone said anything that's just that? No, that's the strange thing. Nobody has. It's all in my head. It's still very real to you? Very. Sorry, last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times. Four times. What was the email about? A change to the behavior policy. It was two paragraphs. I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid. How does he treat you? He has been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted. That makes it worse somehow, because I feel like I'm lying to him. Lying to him about what? About being capable, as if I'm pretending. Pretending to be what? Uh, somebody who knows what she's doing. Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat. That's a vivid image. Whose coat is that? My mum's, I suppose. She was a head teacher for 20 years. Tell me about that. she was brilliant everyone in the village still stops me say what a wonderful head she was she retired six years ago and they have named a library after her and you're now going to similar job? A deputy's job, but yes. I can't help comparing. Everything I do, I think would she have done it better? Does she say that? Never. She is very supportive on the surface. She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly. How does it blend when she says that it makes me feel like i'm making a fuss so i don't tell her how bad it is what does she not know that i'm awake at four every morning i fall asleep fine then i'm awake at four going through the to-do list what is on the list everything timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about. It goes round and round. How long have you been waking like that? Since about the second week of term. I drink a lot of coffee to get for a day which i know doesn't help how many cups uh five or six uh then i can't sit still in the afternoons what do you notice in your body during those afternoons um my heart goes fast my hands are a bit shaky last thursday i had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water did anyone notice I don't think so. I said I was fetching a document. That sounds like a lot of effort to hide it. It is. I am exhausted by the end of every day, just from pretending. Who knows how you're feeling? My partner Ben knows a bit. He says I should just enjoy it. How do you feel when he says that? Guilty and a bit alone. He means well. He's an engineer. He thinks if something's a problem, you fix it. You can't just fix this. No, I wish it were that simple. Do you have friends that go and talk to him? Not anymore, not really. I used to eat lunch in the year 4 quarter with the others. Now I'm their line manager and it's all right. Say it was some company along with the promotion? Yes, I hadn't thought of it like that. I miss them. I miss my class too. What do you miss most? The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time. Now my days are spreadsheets. Do you want a day promotion? I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her. the head. Then I went home and cry. What were the tears about? Fear, I think. And that I would never get to go back. Would you want to go back? I don't know. It sounds terrible, doesn't it? After everyone's been so supportive That sounds like an honest question. Nobody has asked me, Dad. They just say, well, Dan. What was the last time you felt properly relaxed? These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days. What was different, dear? Nobody expected anything of me. I was just talking. Ben carried the sandwiches. Um, yeah. The week before term, I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the sundae. Is there anything you already tried to tell, even let me? I certainly frightened down what went well each evening. Small thing. A chill laughing, a good email. How did that go? It held for about two weeks and then I stopped because I felt silly. Silly in what way? As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging. Probably not. It just felt that way. That sounds worth back coming too. Have you thought about whether there is something particular you would like from our work? I would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud. What would that look like on a Tuesday? Hmm, walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first, sending an email once. And on Sunday? Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots. Those are clear goals. How do you feel now saying them all well? uh lightful lighter a bit tearful actually that's all right take a moment sorry i i didn't expect that there is nothing to apologize for what's coming up That's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows how about the 4am. What would it be like to tell him? Scary. He would probably be heard that I didn't say sooner. Would it be a reason to keep it to yourself? I suppose not. I might try this week. What would help you do that? If I choose a quiet moment, not on a Sunday evening, And then I'm too warmed up. Saturday morning, perhaps? Yeah, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood, Dan. And one more small thing. Would you try the evening notebook again, just for a week? Even one line? I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget. All right, we're nearly out of time. Is there anything you want to add? Only did I nearly cancel this morning. I'm glad I didn't. I'm glad too. Same time next week. Yes, please. Thank you.
